selfCorrection.severity: would have shipped a dead gate
selfCorrection.what: The first version of the honest-empty test was VACUOUS. It asserted that layerEmptyBasis() returns a non-empty string. That accessor falls back to a generic sentence when a registry row declares nothing, so the assertion passes for every row unconditionally and can never fail for the reason it was written.
selfCorrection.howFound: Ran the negative suite before trusting the gate, per DEV_PROCESS 2.2. Deliberately stripped emptyBasis from the ssurgo-soils row and re-ran: 110 tests, 110 pass, 0 fail. The gate did not notice its own subject being removed. The paired ceiling mutation (ceiling: null changed to 254) DID fire, 109 pass / 1 fail, which is what made the silence on the other one legible.
selfCorrection.fix: The assertion now reads entry.emptyBasis on the registry row rather than the accessor's return value. The runtime fallback stays, because a user must never meet silence, but the fallback must not be what ships and only an assertion on the declared field can tell those apart. A second test covers the fallback path so both halves are pinned.
selfCorrection.proofItNowFires: Same mutation re-applied after the fix: 111 tests, 110 pass, 1 fail, failing test 'gives every draws-nothing row a DECLARED basis, not the fallback'. Command exit code 1, read from the command itself and not through a pipe (DEV_PROCESS 2.3).
selfCorrection.note: This is the same defect class as the special-district writer whose verify could never return non-zero. It was caught here only because the negative run happened before the report, not after.

mechanismVerifiedAtSource.claim: Setting spec.visible false actually hides the layer rather than being an inert field.
mechanismVerifiedAtSource.evidence: packages/map-renderer/src/map/overlay-render.js:129-130 computes `const visible = spec.visible !== false` then `const vis = visible ? "visible" : "none"`, and lines 168 / 191 / 216 / 245 apply it via map.setLayoutProperty(id, "visibility", vis) on the UPDATE path as well as at creation. upsertOverlay is idempotent per layerKey, so a toggle updates in place rather than leaking a second layer.
mechanismVerifiedAtSource.whyChecked: A toggle wired to a field the renderer ignores would pass every unit test in this branch and do nothing on a real map. That is the malformed-probe failure the dispatch names.

honestLimitsOfThisVerification: CODE-DONE IS NOT CUSTOMER-DONE. Nothing here is a live probe of a deployed surface. This lane is forbidden to deploy and did not. The road-nodes toggle is verified at the unit level (streetVisible defaults false; the band spec carries visible:false), at the render level (the row and its label appear in static markup), and at the mechanism level (the renderer honours the flag on both paths). It is NOT verified by a human clicking it on a served map. That check belongs to whoever deploys the merge.

The rrc-wells ceiling is RELAYED from the county-ledger's own railCapabilities, re-probed live by this lane. This lane did not independently confirm that the upstream adapter is Harris-only; it quotes the ledger's sourceBasis string and labels it as such.
WRITTEN-layer truth for the RRC rails is not established and is not claimed. No atoms-store access from this repo.

The honest-empty mechanism reads registry declarations. If a layer were wired to a source but declared live:false, it would be labelled empty when it is not. All six affected rows were checked for a fetch path and none has one, but the mechanism's dependence on an accurate declaration is a real constraint, not an assumed-away one. This is the same has_writer-is-hand-declared shape.
